summary: Kenjuro Yanagida was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida around 1921–1924. He later held a post at Hirosaki University.
Kenkai Naganuma was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He held a post at Kurume University and was an emeritus professor at Kyushu University from circa 1947 to 1980.

Kennard Lipman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther (attested 1979) and served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

Kenneth G. Zysk is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who earned an M.A. from UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. from Australian National University. His academic posts include Eastern Michigan University and the University of Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Peking University, Columbia University, Union Theological Seminary, under Aloysius Pieris, and earned a PhD from the CUNY Graduate Center. He held posts at Hunter and Baruch colleges.

Kenneth J. Saunders was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara. He served as Professor of the History of Religion at Pacific School of Religion and lecturer at the University of California (~1921–1935).

Kenneth K. Inada was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and chaired the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research from 1996 to 1999.

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at CSU Hayward, Stanford, the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Toho Gakuin, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley. He held faculty posts at IBS and Musashino University.
Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held an academic post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth de Burgh Codrington was an archaeologist, historian, and Indologist who studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and Wadham College, Oxford. He worked at the Victoria and Albert Museum (~1931–1948) and the University of London (~1948–1965).

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Aichi Gakuin University (2000–2010), the University of Tokyo (professor from 2010), and Rissho University (director in 2025).

Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He earned a doctorate in literature from Otani University and served as professor emeritus at Hanazono University (attested 2014, 2026).
Kenryu Tsuji was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his education at Ryukoku University (1938) and the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Bukkyo University. He was a professor at Koyasan University (1926), Shuchiin University (1955), and Seizan Junior College, later becoming professor emeritus at Ryukoku University (1956).
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Otani University and later served as a professor there (attested 2006).
Kensur Yeshe Thupten is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 1982, he held posts at Middlebury College and as a visiting Tibetan scholar at the University of Virginia.

Kenta Suzuki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1994–1998) and Kyoto University (~1999–2004). He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2013.

Kenyo Mitomo is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and UC Berkeley. He served on the faculty at Rissho University from 1968 to 2015, where he became Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies.

Keshub Chunder Sen was a scholar and figure in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Hindu School, Presidency University (~1854–1858), and the University of Calcutta (~1856–1858), and founded the Brahmo Samaj of India.
